question.value: Does the z=6.63 quasar J0910-0414 trace a galaxy overdensity (protocluster), and how massive is it and what does a nearby double-peaked LAE imply about the quasar lifetime

evidence.quote: In this letter, we report the discovery of a protocluster anchored by a luminous quasar: J0910–0414 at $z=6.63$.
This motivated us to investigate whether J0910–0414 traces an overdensity of galaxies with multi-wavelength followup observations.

referee_caveats_inferred: The ALMA reduction, imaging and line-fitting details are deferred to an in-prep paper, so the [C II] luminosities cannot be checked from this text
Mass estimate depends on extrapolating the Chiang13 formula to z~6.6 and masses beyond its calibration, and on one bias value from Ouchi18
Overdensity of the central region depends on the choice of a ~14x30 arcmin^2 box drawn after seeing the LAE distribution
The lifetime limit uses a single galaxy and ignores peculiar velocity and Lya redshift uncertainty
